name: The roster this runner should carry
description:
Every version this node should be able to play, with the manifest it was admitted under and where its bytes are. `verified` as well as `active`, because a verified version's trial is a real match paired before promotion, and a runner that waited for `active` could never play the trial that produces it.

THE MANIFEST IS REBUILT FIELD BY FIELD, and that is a safety property rather than tidiness. A competitor's manifest can name a `reference` -- the one field that could point outside their own version -- and rebuilding the document key by key leaves it nowhere to survive. `name` becomes the platform's model id for the same reason: Orion takes a model's id from the manifest and a competitor's name is not the platform's. This rebuild MUST stay at the centre; moving it to the edge would put a competitor's bytes back on the path to a node's registration.

tasks.name: Is this runner still live
tasks.description: A separate task rather than a predicate inside the roster query, and soma-models-list is the precedent: json_agg with no GROUP BY answers a row whatever it is fed, so a guard folded into the aggregate would turn a dead runner into an empty roster -- which reads as 'register nothing' and is indistinguishable from a quiet ladder.

input.query: SELECT lr.id AS runner_ok FROM live_runners lr WHERE lr.id = ($1)::uuid

with.name: No live runner
with.description: A revoked key, a revoked runner or a demoted owner. 401 rather than 403 because the runner's correct response is to exchange its key again, and that is what a 401 tells it to do.

tasks.name: Stamp the runner as seen
tasks.description: The roster tick is the runner's heartbeat -- it is the one call it makes whether or not there is anything to play -- so last_seen_at is stamped here rather than on the claim, where an idle poll would be doing the same work 0.8 times a second.

input.query: UPDATE runners SET last_seen_at = now() WHERE id = ($1)::uuid AND last_seen_at < now() - interval '30 seconds'
